newsitem.title: USA: J.C.Penney debt deal raised to meet demand.
newsitem.headline: J.C.Penney debt deal raised to meet demand.

text.p: J.C. Penney & Co Inc's multi-tranche debt offering has been increased to $2.3 billion from $2.0 billion, and an additional three-year maturity has been added, dealers said Wednesday.
They cited growing investor demand for the issue, originally a five-part offering.
They said the offering was seen issue-bid across all tranches, leading most to believe the deal would have to be increased again to meet demand.
"The Penney deal was restructured to include a $300 million three-year tranche which is expected to come at a spread of 40 to 45 basis points over Treasuries," one dealer said.
"Talk in the market is that the deal may go higher than the $2.3 billion," said another dealer. "We're hearing that the five-year tranche may be upped in size as well."
The six-part $2.3 billion debt offering, to be launched later this morning, includes the following tranches, dealers said.
-- $300 million of a three-year issue seen priced at 40-45 basis points over Treasuries.
-- $600 million of a five-year issue seen priced at 45-50 basis points over Treasuries.
-- $400 million of a 10-year issue seen priced at 70 basis points over Treasuries.
-- $300 million in 20-year debt seen priced at 85 basis points over Treasuries.
-- $350 million of 30-year bonds, callable after 10 years, seen priced in the 120 basis points area.
-- $350 million of 40-year bonds, putable in eight years, seen priced in the mid-40s basis points range.
Market players said the deal has plenty of room to grow as Penney currently has about $3.0 billion in debt on the shelf.
Credit Suisse First Boston is expected to serve as lead underwriter for the offering.
